chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Regarding a man who bought from another man a slave or an animal, and stipulated one day or two days; then the slave died, or the animal perished, or some incident occurred in it—upon whom is the liability?
He said: There is no liability upon the buyer until the condition period ends and the sold item becomes his.

key_terms.الضَّمَانُ: liability or financial responsibility for loss
key_terms.شَرَطَ: stipulated a condition in the sale
key_terms.يَنْقَضِيَ: comes to an end or expires
key_terms.يَوْمًا: a day, referring here to the option period

ai.seo_question: Who bears liability if a sold animal or slave is damaged during the option period of a sale?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling about liability during a stipulated option period in a sale. If the sold slave or animal dies, perishes, or develops a defect before the condition period expires, the buyer is not liable until that period ends and the sale becomes fully binding upon him.
